challenge.intro: Each team runs a car-transport desk for one simulated week in Finland. The final is one secret week; the ten ranked teams with the highest margin present to a jury.

steps.title: Dealers ask for prices
steps.text: From Monday to Friday, car dealers send price requests: one car, or two in a trade-in, to move between towns. Each request offers delivery options — same day, next day, within 3 days — each with a deadline and a public list price. You have 15 minutes to quote.

steps.title: You quote, the dealer chooses
steps.text: Every request also goes to a house competitor, priced 26–54% above the list price in the final's level. The dealer compares your price with the competitor's and with the value of speed — and buys from you, or from them. A win is an order with a deadline.

steps.title: Freelance drivers move the cars
steps.text: You post gigs in the drivers' app: a fee, a fee schedule, and up to three cars per gig. A driver books when the fee beats their costs — their time, their trips, their evening. They can drop a booking; drivers learn whether waiting brings a higher fee.

steps.title: Margin, minus refunds
steps.text: Margin = your prices − driver fees − late refunds. A car up to 2 hours late refunds 10% of its price; more than two business days late refunds all of it. A car nobody delivers costs twice its price.

steps.title: The 90% rule
steps.text: A team is ranked only when at least 90% of its orders arrive on time. Winning work is easier than delivering it — the whole game is how much profitable work you can still promise. The final ranks the top 10 by margin; a jury then judges the approach: elegant, clear, creative, robust.

words: Dealer
a car-dealer site that sends price requests
Request
one or two cars to move, with delivery options and a response deadline 15 minutes after it arrives
Option
a delivery promise: same_day, next_day or within_3_days, each with its own deadline and list price
List price
the public price list by distance — not the competitor's price
Quote
your price for each option you offer; the dealer decides at the response deadline
Order
a request you won, with a deadline
Gig
the job you post in the drivers' app: stops, a window, a fee schedule
Fee
what you pay the driver; it may rise on a schedule
Typical fee
the request's reference fee — about what a driver is usually paid for the work
Deadline
20:00 on a business day; on time means every leg delivered by it
Margin
prices in, driver fees, refunds and penalties out

parts.name: The desk
parts.reason: Keeps the books — requests, orders, gigs, bookings, deliveries — so every decision uses the same account of the week.
parts.effect: Practice and the live final run the same desk, so what we measure is what we play.

parts.name: The note reader
parts.reason: Turns a dealer's note — in Finnish, Swedish or English — into constraints before a failed visit teaches the same lesson.
parts.effect: Reads ready times, release after payment, pickup and delivery hours, deadlines, manual licences, plates, corrections. The world enforces what notes say; its full effect was never isolated.

parts.name: The intake
parts.reason: Protects delivery capacity before we promise it away: at most 45 orders without a booked driver (55 before noon), a safe-car allowance to 100, and 12 hours of slack after the first car's drive.
parts.effect: The volume step (safe cars + flat fees): +€69,993 (+14.3%) over 40 paired weeks, better in 38 of 40, 364 orders a week instead of 277.

parts.name: The cost model
parts.reason: Gradient-boosted trees on 44 inputs known at quote time — the lane, the hour, the cars, the note, our own books — trained on 1.9 million won orders; prices each car's expected fee (as a multiple of the typical fee) and its late risk.
parts.effect: The learned model over the hand-fit one: +€32,271 over 40 paired weeks, and the worst weeks rose (rob-17 90.2% → 95.4%). The final week's model (5) was kept for its safer floor on unseen worlds.

parts.name: The quoter
parts.reason: Learns what dealers will pay: one level per market that rises after wins and falls after losses, plus each dealer's trust (+1% per on-time order, up to 25); quotes the price that maximises (price − cost) × chance to win.
parts.effect: Quoting same-day whenever 8 hours of slack remain, with the cost tilt that keeps marginal cars out: +€31,975 over 40 weeks.

parts.name: The fees
parts.reason: A gig opens at what the model expects the car to cost, minus 15%, floored at 0.75 of the typical fee (0.95 for the shortest lanes) — and holds it: one step after 6 hours, one more a day before the last pickup, none at night.
parts.effect: The evening fix that came out of this very test final: +€31,187 over 40 paired weeks, holdout +€10,243, better in 34 of 40.

parts.name: The bundles
parts.reason: Up to three single-car orders share one gig at 0.85 of the sum of their fees, when the route fits; a bundle still without a driver splits after 120 minutes.
parts.effect: The same cars booked for €916 together against €1,068 alone in 11 paired probes — 14% less. Bundles of 4 or 5 lost money.

parts.name: The repairs
parts.reason: Keep cars moving and stop paying urgent fees when timeliness is already lost: windows that ended, orphaned cars without a gig, and calm pricing for cars already past their last pickup.
parts.effect: calm: +€6,163 over 40 paired weeks, accepted with the honest tradeoff that it touches only cars that are already late.

method: Every idea is a switch; the mainline with the switch off must reproduce the previous adopted label to the cent before a comparison counts.
Every comparison replays the same worlds — 10 dev, 20 rob, 10 holdout — with both versions; the world is deterministic, so one run per version suffices.
A change is an improvement only when total margin rises and no week drops out of the ranking.
A change that drops any week under the 90% rule, or lowers the lowest weeks, is not adopted — however much margin it adds.

adoption.label: Safe-car intake + flat fees
adoption.note: +14.3%, 38/40 weeks better, 364 vs 277 orders a week

adoption.label: Same-day at 8 h slack + cost tilt
adoption.note: 31/40 better; same-day alone lost a week (89.2%)

adoption.label: Lower fee floors + short-lane tilt
adoption.note: the evening fix after this test final; holdout +€10,243

adoption.label: Retrained model (4) + tilt 1.1
adoption.note: fee error 0.165 vs 0.183 on recent weeks

adoption.label: Model 5 (safer floor)
adoption.note: in-sample +€14,444; on the 30 worlds it never trained on −€1,875 (money-neutral) — kept for the safer weakest weeks: 92.4% vs 91.8%

adoption.label: Higher limits 45/55/100
adoption.note: positive on every set, including unseen worlds (b87; holdout +€4,033)
